title.narrative: UN Women i Bangladesh - stöd till SN 2024-2027
UN Women in Bangladesh - support to SN 2024-2027

description.narrative:
Stöd till UN Womens strategiska not 2022-2027 för perioden aug 2024-dec 2027, som har 5 mål: 1) Inkluderande och hållbar ekonomisk utveckling 2) Jämställdhetsmedveten motståndskraft mot klimatförändringar, chocker och katastrofer 3) Stoppa våldet mot kvinnor 4) Transformativ, deltagande och inkluderande styrning 5) Insatser för att stärka beslutsfattande och egenmakt av kvinnor och flickor från rohingya- och värdsamhällen i Cox's Bazar
Sverige kommer att särskilt följa upp kontinuiteten av målområden 2 och 5, med fokus på stärkande av jämställdhetsmedveten resiliens och motståndskraft mot klimatförändringar och katastrofer samt rohingya-insatser.

Support to UN Women's Strategic Note 2022-2027 for the period Aug 2024-Dec 2027, which has 5 outcomes: 1) Inclusive and sustainable economic development 2) Gender-responsive resilience to climate change, shocks and disasters 3) Ending violence against women 4) Transformative, participatory and inclusive governance 5) Gender-responsive enabling environment in the Rohingya refugee response in Cox's Bazar
While Sweden will particularly follow-up on continuity of outcomes 2 and 5, focusing on gender-responsive resilience and the Rohingya refugee response, UN Women may channel funding to sustain critical programming interventions across its other priorities.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The first year of funding to UN Women's Strategic Note, coinciding with the historic political transition in Bangladesh, enabled UN Women to remain agile in responding to emerging issues, while sustaining its longstanding efforts to foreground gender equality and women's rights across the humanitarian-development-peace continuum, including those aligned to ongoing national reform and transitional processes.
In a year when Bangladesh was ravaged by four devastating climate-related disasters, UN Women played a crucial role in mainstreaming gender equality considerations into humanitarian action, leveraging its strong partnerships with Women's Rights Organizations (WRO) and Women-Led Organizations (WLO). As co-chair of the national Gender in Humanitarian Action (GiHA) working group led by the Department of Women's Affairs (DWA), UN Women facilitated data and analysis generated with support from local WLOs to inform the Humanitarian Response Plan in 2024. To advance localization efforts, UN Women successfully advocated for the establishment of three new district-level GiHA chapters in Jamalpur, Khulna and Satkhira. UN Women ensured that the local chapters are co-chaired by a government (local DWA units) and a women-led civil society representative, thereby generating ownership of key stakeholders in the GiHA mechanism. Another significant milestone was the formation of a national Women's Climate Action Network with 100 Women-Led Organisations (WLOs) from the five most climate-vulnerable districts (Cox's Bazar, Jamalpur, Khulna, Kurigram and Satkhira).
Against increased insecurities, GBV incidents, and the arrival of several thousands of Rohingya fleeing the armed conflict in Myanmar, the self-mobilization of Rohingya women to assert their rights and leadership demonstrated the most progress in Cox's Bazar. Amid men's forced recruitment, Rohingya women exercised agency and leadership, many assuming sole responsibility for their families, some organizing into groups to protect their camps from violent groups. High numbers of women pursued protection and empowerment services, despite mobility restrictions.
Addressing the critical lack of essential literacy and numeracy skills among adults, 2024 saw the introduction of Accelerated Adult Learning (AAL) in the camps. Contributing to these results, the 53 UN Women supported Rohingya Gender Volunteers adopted expanded roles, monitoring gendered insecurities, accompanying women and girls to essential services and providing psychosocial support, reaching 51,566 Rohingya women and men and facilitating 5,652 service referrals in six camps.
Services provided at the 8 Multi-Purpose Women's Centres (MPWCs) enhanced the resilience and empowerment of 120,524 women and girls in 2024 (Rohingya: 97,591 and host community: 22,933).
With decreased funding available for the Joint Response Plan (JRP), UN Women support contributed to increased visibility of refugee and women-led solutions as an effective means to ensure longer-term sustainability of the response, and to access gender analysis, and enhanced capacities of WROs and humanitarian actors.
UN Women transitioned operations of 5 MPWCs to 3 local WROs (JNUS and their consortium partner SKUS took on the responsibility of operating 2 MPWCs while RWWS managed the operations of three MPWCs). ActionAid Bangladesh continued to operate 3 MPWCs and assisted the localization process by hosting GBV case management and AAL trainings for new partners. For the first time, local WROs were recognized as UN Women programme partners under the Livelihoods and Skills Development Sector in the 2025-2026 Joint Response Plan (JRP). This inclusion signifies an important milestone in the contribution of local WROs to humanitarian response.
To support a standardized approach, UN Women developed guidance on operating MPWCs through an integrated service model based on feminist principes and international norms and standards.
The GiHA working group continued to play a pivotal role in enhancing the gender mainstreaming capacities and skills of humanitarian actors across sectors to address the critical needs of Rohingya refugee and host community women and girls in Cox's Bazar.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
